1. Choke the well back until the recommended maximum rate is observed and monitor acoustic sand detector readings.

column15:
1. If possible, open the choke (in slow and small incremental steps) to increase the gas flow rate above its predetermined minimum alarm set point. 

2. If the choke is already fully open, monitor the amount of water being produced via the wet gas flow meter and if necessary recalculate the liquid hold up expected. 

3. If acceptable or the well is naturally at end of life plateau either clear the alarm and closely monitor the production or deselect the alarm if satisfied that no possible increase in production is likely from the well.

Note: this could be an indication of misdirected flow from the manifold.

column15:
1. Check alternative sensors (PTT2) to ascertain if alarm is genuine (i.e. not spurious)

2. Check nearest functional downstream temperature gauge and follow Operating Guidelines (especially during cold well start-up).

3. If alarm is genuine, the line should be isolated between the well and manifold whilst the cause of the temperature excursion is established.
Note: The most likely cause of low temperatures is a high pressure differential across the choke coupled with a low gas velocity. This can occur if there is a sudden drop in downstream pressure i.e., from manifold. As a result it is likely that more than one well will experience lower than normal temperature excursions and should therefore be monitored accordingly.

4. If alarm is spurious, log in control room daily log and clear alarm.

1. Check alternative sensors (PTT2) to ascertain if alarm is genuine (i.e. not spurious)

2. Check nearest functional downstream temperature gauge and follow Operating Guidelines (especially during cold well start-up).

3. If alarm is genuine, the line should be isolated between the well and manifold whilst the cause of the temperature excursion is established.
Note: The most likely cause of low temperatures is a high pressure differential across the choke coupled with a low gas velocity. This can occur if there is a sudden drop in downstream pressure i.e., from manifold. As a result it is likely that more than one well will experience lower than normal temperature excursions and should therefore be monitored accordingly.

4. If alarm is spurious, log in control room daily log and clear alarm.

1. Check alternative sensors (PTT2) to ascertain if alarm is genuine (i.e. not spurious)

2. Check nearest functional downstream temperature gauge and follow Operating Guidelines (especially during cold well start-up).

3. If alarm is genuine, the line should be isolated between the well and manifold whilst the cause of the temperature excursion is established.
Note: The most likely cause of low temperatures is a high pressure differential across the choke coupled with a low gas velocity. This can occur if there is a sudden drop in downstream pressure i.e., from manifold. As a result it is likely that more than one well will experience lower than normal temperature excursions and should therefore be monitored accordingly.

4. If alarm is spurious, log in control room daily log and clear alarm.

column33:
1. Collection pot will be filled and pressurized according to time left by
operator without the action.

2. It may lead to limited mechanical damage in case of prolonged periods
and may lead to replacing mechanical seal.
3. Installed orifice at the pot vent (3.2mm hole diameter) will allow
condensate and vapor to escape to atmosphere.

Notes:
1. According to mechanical seal design, design pressure is (40 barg) which
is higher than pump maximum pressure (11 barg)
Therefore, there will be no effect on mechanical integrity of the mechanical
seal system.
2. There should be a pressure transmitter in place according to OEM manual
to indicate higher pressure (recommended set point is 0.7 barg according to
API 682). That aligns with having the installed RO in place.
